decisions.summary: Guard by guard with shell and settings entry removed in the registering commit (D3/FR-003); suite as verdict replay with its inline Python replaced in the same task (D4); order by measured cost first (R2); the two XIV fixes on make-only-hooks and guard-file-hooks (FR-002's exception).
decisions.why: Each is settled by the accepted spec (D3, D4, FR-002's named exception, FR-003) and none is T006's own: the XIV fixes belong to two other guards' tasks, so T006 changes no expected verdict. Putting pair-hooks first agrees with m:hooks-bash, which names it the slowest guard.

decisions.summary: The Rust decider keeps consulting the eight phase-3 Python tools (checkpoint.py, plan_gate.py, review_prereq.py, review_owed.py, gate-stamp.py, make engine-key, hm_arbiter.py, hm_dropped.py) by path on its two rare branches and at Stop, until each tool's own port answers in-process.
decisions.why: FR-001 fixes the phase order (hooks first, tooling in phase 3) and FR-003 requires a piece's Python to stay the one that runs until its replacement passes, so a hook ported in phase 1 has to call the tooling that is still Python. FR-007 asks for one guard process per tool call, not one per guard. It does not forbid the guard calling external tools, and the plain Bash path that SC-001/m:hooks-bash measures reaches none of them. This is temporary sequencing the spec requires, not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: The engine key (a find over l7r/ and pool/, plus make engine-key when the cache is stale) is computed only on the two branches that read it, not on every call.
decisions.why: Removing work that changes no verdict serves the request's purpose (the GM: the Python code is too inefficient), and FR-002's suite replay gates it. Two notes that are not rulings: (1) the citation is stretched, because FR-006 names three specific fixes and the plan's paraphrase 'a fact computed once, and only where it is used' is broader than the text; (2) today every call has a side effect, refreshing the cached key, and the claim that 'no other branch reads it' is shown only by the suite. If anything outside pair-hooks reads that cache and relies on the per-call refresh, FR-002's 'outputs' would cover it. Whether anything does was not measured in this bundle.

decisions.summary: The guard's inline Python state handling (pairing state, review rounds, dispatch record, bypass log, read_field) becomes Rust over the same files and formats.
decisions.why: This is the port FR-001 asks for, and keeping the same files and formats is what FR-002's same-outputs rule requires.

decisions.summary: The suite's "$HOOK" pretool|stop runs l7r-guard --only pair-hooks PreToolUse|Stop through a shared shim tests/hooks/guard-shim.sh, with the suite's cases unchanged.
decisions.why: This is D4 as written: the suite points at l7r-guard --only <guard> and its cases are unchanged. The shim only maps the suite's existing argument form onto the binary's.

decisions.summary: Green: the suite passes against the Rust guard, plus rust-test, cover and hooks-test. Red: record the failure and stop to make arbiter-ask. Landed by make land-tooling with no work budget.
decisions.why: The exits restate FR-002/FR-003/FR-004's gates, and the landing route is process that narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: hm_make.py's targets, combine and classify-through-bare-pytest move to rust/guard/src/shared/make.rs with gate-hooks, patterns verbatim; the rest of hm_make.py moves with make-only-hooks (T028) and guard-file-hooks (T029).
decisions.why: Partitions a shared library across the guards that read it; every part is still ported (FR-001, the request's 'all be ported to Rust'), verbatim patterns keep FR-002's same verdicts, and the suite replay (D4) checks the result. Nothing is left in Python that the request or spec would have ported.

decisions.summary: The decider reads tool_input.command as JSON instead of the shell's greedy sed, so a ' -k ' in the description field no longer arms the subset flag; a suite case is added, the fix named in the commit and the phase's record.
decisions.why: Applies the one exception the accepted FR-002 already states - a guard refusing correct work (a later make done refused on a falsely armed subset flag) is fixed in its port under constitution XIV - with that exception's conditions met: the case lands in the same commit and the change is named in the commit and the phase's record. It narrows nothing the GM asked for; the request is to make the codebase Rust, not to preserve a misparse.

decisions.summary: gate-hooks.sh's status mode is ported: l7r-guard --only gate-hooks status prints the same subset_pending= line, reached through the shim's status mode.
decisions.why: Preserves an existing output as FR-002 requires (same verdicts and outputs); it reverses the dropping the earlier preflight ruled NOT LEGITIMATE.

decisions.summary: After T005, independent of the other guards; green exit is the suite against l7r-guard --only gate-hooks plus rust-test, cover and hooks-test; the shell and its settings entry go in the commit that registers the decider.
decisions.why: Restates D3 (guard by guard, never both, FR-003) and D4 (the suite is the replay), and FR-004's coverage floor; no new scope.

decisions.summary: The sanitized command and the last full gate are read in-process; gatecost.py (asked only on a streak's first expensive measurement, for its reminder's median) stays the measure tool's, asked by path, until phase 3 ports it.
decisions.why: FR-001 orders the port in four phases and FR-003 keeps a piece's Python the one that runs until its replacement passes; gatecost.py belongs to a later phase, so calling it where the shell did is what those require, not a carve-out from them. It is not a guard, so FR-007's one process per tool call is not touched. Nothing the guard decides is left out of the port.

decisions.summary: The shell's greedy read (from the payload's last "command" key to its last quote) is kept for the git commit reset only, reproduced over the input in its own key order.
decisions.why: FR-002 requires the same verdicts as the shell on every suite case, and its only exception (XIV) is for a guard that refuses correct work. A later field naming git commit RESETS the streak, which makes the guard more permissive, so it refuses nothing correct, and the exception does not reach it. Keeping the shell's behavior is FR-002 applied as written. Reproducing the span over the re-serialized input rather than the raw bytes is a design choice; FR-002 judges it on the suite's cases, which the exits require to pass.

decisions.summary: status is ported, printing the same measurements_since_reset=N budget=B line.
decisions.why: FR-002: same outputs as the piece replaced.

decisions.summary: The shell guard and its settings entry are removed in the commit that registers the Rust decider, after test-measure-hooks.sh passes against l7r-guard --only measure-hooks.
decisions.why: Plan D3/D4 and FR-003 (never both), stated as accepted.

decisions.summary: hm_shape.py's wait/sleep/watch/self-matching/ceiling/periodic-report functions move to rust/guard/src/shared/wait.rs with each pattern verbatim; the rest of hm_shape.py (executing_backticks) moves with the guard that reads it
decisions.why: FR-001 replaces every tracked Python file and D3 moves guards one by one; porting the library the guard reads, patterns verbatim, is how FR-002's same-verdicts requirement is met. Nothing is left in Python or dropped - the remainder is assigned to its own guard's port.

decisions.summary: the periodic-report refusal's cron minute stays the local minute, read via `date +%M` only on the backgrounded-periodic-report branch
decisions.why: Keeps the Python's verdict and output (time.localtime().tm_min) exactly, which is what FR-002 requires; the earlier UTC alternative was the deviation and is already rejected. A child process on one rare branch is a mechanism choice, not a second guard process (FR-007 is about one process per tool call for the guards), and it changes nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: self_matching compiles the command's pgrep -f pattern with fancy-regex instead of Python re, skips a pattern it cannot compile as the Python skipped one re could not, and rests dialect-divergence detection on the suite replay
decisions.why: FR-002 scopes equivalence to every case the tests and suites hold, and D4 makes the suite the replay; the decision meets that bound, preserves the skip-on-uncompilable behavior, and states plainly that divergence outside the suite is not covered - which is the spec's own bound, not a carve-out from it. A Rust port cannot use Python's re, so a different engine is inherent to the request.

decisions.summary: The verdict library scripts/hooks/lib/hm_tree.py (judge, explain, log context) is ported whole, each pattern verbatim, to rust/guard/src/shared/tree.rs, shared with gm-tree-hooks, which moves to it in its own task.
decisions.why: FR-001 replaces every Python file and FR-002 asks for the same verdicts; porting the library the verdict comes from, verbatim, is how the guard is ported. Done-measured deletes only main-tree-hooks.sh and its settings entry, so hm_tree.py stays for gm-tree-hooks until that guard's own replacement passes (FR-003, D3).

decisions.summary: The session's clone comes from T003's session facts through the same resolver ported (claim map, last /rename, sessions json), not from spawning clone-sync-hooks.sh resolve.
decisions.why: The same resolution with the same inputs, run in the one guard process FR-007 requires; FR-002's suite replay (D4) checks the verdicts.

decisions.summary: The mirror root comes from walking up to the nearest .git (T006's find_root) and cutting at /.clones/, not from git rev-parse --show-toplevel.
decisions.why: A mechanism change stated to give the same answer, which the suite replay must confirm before the switch (FR-002, D4). It narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: The refusal and the rewrite's context name rust/guard/src/guards/main_tree_hooks.rs instead of scripts/hooks/main-tree-hooks.sh, which this task deletes; no verdict changes.
decisions.why: This is an exception to FR-002's 'same outputs', and the only exception FR-002 names is the XIV fix, so it is judged as a carve-out. Applied literally, the rule would make the guard send a refused session to a file this same commit deletes. That defeats what the message is for, which is telling the reader where the rule lives. It does not reach what FR-002 is for, proving the port changes no decision, because only the self-referencing path changes and every verdict and all other text stay as they are. The precedent is T006. If a suite case asserts the path, its expected text changes in the same commit and the commit must name that change.

decisions.summary: The hook half of scripts/measure/event_log.py (line, verdict reading, categories, log path, append) moves into the Rust decider with patterns, fields and order verbatim; the from-transcript command stays Python until phase 3 ports the measure tools.
decisions.why: The request is to make the codebase Rust; FR-001 orders the port in phases with the hooks first. The code that runs on every hook event is the hook's, and porting it with the guard is the hooks phase doing its job. The part that is a command, not a hook, goes in the later measure-tools phase, which FR-001's phase order already provides; nothing is excluded from the port. Keeping the line's fields and order the same is what FR-002 requires so that feature-report reads it unchanged.

decisions.summary: On an Edit, the reversal test (hm_arbiter.reversal) runs in-process in Rust; recording the trip is handed to hm_arbiter.py by path, and only when a reversal is found, until the arbiter is ported.
decisions.why: The arbiter is its own piece in FR-001's phase order, and this block does not port it. Calling it by path, and only on the rare reversal, keeps Python off the common path, which is the hook start-up cost the GM's request was about, and it lasts only until the arbiter's own port, so no Python is kept for good. FR-003 is per piece: the guard's verdict comes from Rust alone, so no piece runs both. The block follows T006 (a).

decisions.summary: The log line's ev is taken from the payload's hook_event_name, as the Python did; l7r-guard --only with no event name reads it from the payload, so the suite's "$HOOK" replays unchanged.
decisions.why: This keeps the Python's behavior (FR-002) and lets the guard's existing suite replay against the Rust guard without edits (D4). It is an interface detail that serves the spec and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The edit digest stays SHA-1's first 12 hex digits, written as a small SHA-1 in shared beside T006's SHA-256 rather than taken from a crate.
decisions.why: Keeping the digest format is FR-002 (same outputs). Writing the hash in shared rather than using a crate is a design choice, not a fidelity question, and it narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: The tools the guard asks (git, sync-with-main.sh, own-make.sh, gate_lock.py, clone_local_settings.py, solo.py, usage_log.py, layout_carry.sh) stay theirs and are asked by path until their own ports.
decisions.why: The request ports all the Python and the spec phases it (FR-001); FR-003 requires the Python to remain the one that runs until its replacement passes. Each tool is named as ending at its own port, so this is order, not an exclusion.

decisions.summary: The session facts the guard's inline Python read (input fields, canonical clone, whether another claimant is live) are read in-process from T003's facts and /proc; the notice's make targets use shared::make::targets.
decisions.why: This is the port itself, what the request asks for; the block binds it to the same answers, which is FR-002.

decisions.summary: The script stays as its resolve mode only, code unchanged and outside l7r-guard, until T051 deletes its callers; prompt and pretool leave in this task.
decisions.why: Sequencing, not a carve-out: (1) the kept code has a named remover, T051, so nothing is excluded from the port the request asks for and FR-001 phases; (2) the guard runs on one path, since resolve is not a guard mode and both guard modes and both settings entries go in the commit that registers the decider (item 9, D3), so FR-003 is met; (3) FR-002 is untouched, the resolve code being unchanged. The not-through-l7r-guard reasoning (recursion, cargo build) is mechanism and decides nothing here either way. Two points for the record: step 1 says 'its shell gone' while (c) keeps the script, and item 9 is the operative statement; and (b) ports the canonical-clone lookup while (c) keeps the shell's canonical_clone for the other guards, so two implementations are live until T051. That is not FR-003's 'both', each call taking one path, but T051 owes the deletion of the shell's version as well as of its callers.

decisions.summary: The prompt mode's lines are the decider's plain-stdout answer, byte for byte, so the suite's prompt cases pass unedited.
decisions.why: Directly FR-002: same outputs, suite expectations unedited.

decisions.summary: Every mode (stop, prompt, timer, stagger) moves to Rust; the detached wait and printed stagger become the binary's --idle-tests entry, started by setsid nohup as the shell was; the GM's disable of 2026-09-06 carries over as one constant, arming off.
decisions.why: Porting every mode is what the GM's 'making this a Rust codebase' and D3 ask, and leaves no shell behind. Keeping arming off is FR-002 (same verdicts), not a carve-out. FR-007's one process concerns the guards deciding a tool call, not a background wait started the way the shell started it.

decisions.summary: git, setsid, nohup, kill, pgrep and the run itself stay external tools asked by path; the lock is the flock tool on the lock file's descriptor.
decisions.why: These are system tools, not Python or shell in the repository, so FR-001 is untouched and nothing the GM asked for is reduced. The stated semantics (a lock owned by the open file the timer holds, as fd 9 was) keep FR-002. The choice of flock tool over a library call is design, which this mode does not grade.

decisions.summary: The small tools and the Python fragments go in-process (field, state_of, JSON, cksum with the same CRC values, ls -t, clone top); the JSON's keys and values are the same, its key order and indentation are not held.
decisions.why: FR-002 binds outputs 'on every case its tests and its suites hold'. Key order and indentation are outside that unless a case holds them, and if one does the block's own exit (every case of the suite passes, expectations unedited but the one in d-2) fails and the task is set down, so the obligation is not reduced. The request says nothing of byte layout. The premise that each reader takes it by key could not be checked from the bundle; the exit, not the premise, is what keeps this within.

decisions.summary: $HOOK stagger <name> reaches --idle-tests through the shim.
decisions.why: D4 points HOOK at the Rust guard; the shim routes the case's unchanged input to the entry of (a). No expectation moves.

decisions.summary: The case 'the shipped default IS disabled' grepped the shell's DEF_ARM=0; it reads the Rust constant instead.
decisions.why: This edits a case of the suite D4 makes the replay and FR-002 holds, so it is ruled on, not passed as within. The general rule is physically impossible here: the case greps a file the port must delete (D3, the GM's move to Rust), so it cannot pass unedited once the shell is gone. The case's purpose survives whole: it pins the GM's disable where that disable now lives, and its expected result is unchanged, so this is not FR-002's verdict-change exception and needs no XIV fix. It covers this one case; the block states every other expectation is unedited.

decisions.summary: Every mode of agent-stall-hooks is ported: prompt becomes the guard; check, watch, pending and ack become the binary's --agent-stall, with the Python scan done in-process and one read of each transcript's last line.
decisions.why: A complete port, which is what the request and FR-001 ask, with FR-002's same outputs. Read as: the scan the embedded Python did is now Rust code inside the Rust process. If it instead meant the binary still runs Python, it would contradict the request and FR-001; the block's goal and its 'script's logic gone' support the port reading, and the repository was not opened to confirm it.

decisions.summary: scripts/hooks/agent-stall-hooks.sh stays until T051 as a forwarder holding only a call to l7r-guard.sh --agent-stall, because this guard's report and engine-freeze-hooks' refusal print that path and sessions run watch by hand; its hook mode leaves the settings in this task (with item 9, the done-condition).
decisions.why: Does not narrow what was asked. The request and FR-001 replace Python with Rust; the forwarder is one line of shell and no Python runs. FR-003: the forwarder runs only Rust, so no piece runs both. D3 requires the settings entry to leave in the decider's commit, which the block does, and says nothing of deleting the file. FR-002: the printed command is an output, and keeping the path keeps it true. Removal at T051 is sequencing, not scope; T051's content is outside this bundle and was not checked. FR-005 (make the one entry point) is not cited by the block, but this is a hand-run path sessions already use, not a new one. Item 1's 'its shell gone' is looser than item 9, which states the actual condition; a wording tension in the plan, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: watch still loops until killed; a tick count from the environment ends it for a unit test; the seams AGENT_STALE_S, AGENT_RECENT_S and AGENT_TICK_S are kept.
decisions.why: The tick count exists only so a test of an endless loop can meet FR-008; with FR-008 gone it has no purpose. watch's behavior is unchanged when it is unset, and keeping the existing seams serves FR-002 and D4.

decisions.summary: Ordering: after T005, in the plan's order, independent of the other guards.
decisions.why: D3's guard-by-guard order after the dispatcher lands; FR-001 puts the hooks first.

decisions.summary: Exits: the guard's suite green against l7r-guard --only agent-stall-hooks, make rust-test and cover green, make hooks-test green; on red, record and stop to make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: D4's replay as the switch condition, FR-002 and FR-003, and FR-004's coverage floor. The red exit is process and changes nothing asked.

decisions.summary: Lands by make land-tooling with no work budget, nothing rolled.
decisions.why: Landing mechanics for tooling; it does not touch any requirement or the request.

decisions.summary: lib/stall_watchdog.py (the pass) is ported to stall_watchdog_hooks/pass.rs with the shell; prompt is the guard, run and once are the binary's --stall-watchdog
decisions.why: FR-001 puts scripts/hooks/ and the libraries its guards call in phase 1, and the GM asked for all the Python to be ported. This resolves round 1's BLOCKED on keeping the file in Python. Item 9's measured Done names the shell and settings entry but not the .py; that is an omission and not a decision to keep it, since (a) states the port and FR-001's phase-end census refuses a survivor.

decisions.summary: Each loop pass still starts a fresh process through the wrapper, so an update to what a stall is reaches a running loop
decisions.why: Keeps the existing behavior under FR-002. The block does not name the wrapper; items 1 and 9 (shell and settings entry gone) constrain it to the Rust binary's entry, and nothing in the text retains the Python.

decisions.summary: The Rust loop still asks finished-run-hooks.sh live by path until T017 moves it
decisions.why: D3 moves guards one per commit, so a mixed interim is the approved order. FR-003 is per piece: this piece has one runner and the other guard has one runner. The dependency is named and bounded by T017.

decisions.summary: kill -0 becomes the /proc/<pid> check; the one-instance lock is T014's flock moved to shared::tool, its descriptor closed for children by default; the sleep is in-process
decisions.why: Implementation choices inside a port. FR-002's equality is enforced by the exit that every suite case passes against the Rust guard.

decisions.summary: The guard does nothing when L7R_SELF_CHECK is set, which main.rs's self-check sandbox sets
decisions.why: The one except-when in the section, adjudicated as such. FR-002's domain is every case the tests and suites hold; --self-check is a harness of the Rust build that the block says the shell never faced, and the variable is set by that sandbox alone, so no suite case or real prompt reaches the branch. It removes no behavior the GM or the spec asked for. The exit requires every suite case green against the Rust guard without that variable.

decisions.summary: The loop ends if its state directory disappears, so a loop started under a suite's moved HOME does not run for ever
decisions.why: An added end condition on a directory-less loop, not a verdict or an output of any case FR-002 covers; if the suite held a contrary case, the exit would fail. It does not touch what the watchdog is for: the block states the real state directory is never removed, and the guard on the prompt path is what starts the loop.

decisions.summary: A count of passes from the environment ends run for a unit test, as T015's (c); STALL_PERIOD and STALL_STATE_DIR kept
decisions.why: A test seam that serves FR-008 and adds no behavior outside the tests; the two existing variables are retained under FR-002.

decisions.summary: Sequence after T005, independent of the other guards; exits are the guard's suite against l7r-guard --only, make rust-test, cover and make hooks-test; shell and settings entry gone in the commit that registers the decider; landed by make land-tooling
decisions.why: D3 and D4 as the spec states them, with FR-004's coverage floor carried by cover.

decisions.id: (a) every mode and all its Python ported
decisions.summary: prompt and stop become the guard; check, seen, live, judge and stale become the binary's --finished-run; the inline Python moves in-process with its rules unchanged.
decisions.why: This is the whole of the piece, nothing left in Python: the GM's 'all be ported to Rust', FR-001 and FR-002.

decisions.id: (a)-proc every process fact from /proc, never a pattern over the hook's own command line
decisions.summary: How process facts are read in the port.
decisions.why: An implementation means, stated under 'rules unchanged'. FR-002 binds its verdicts on every suite case, and D4's replay in exit 6 settles that by run; if a verdict moved, FR-002's XIV path would have to name it, and the block claims none.

decisions.id: (a)-T016 the watchdog pass asks live in-process
decisions.summary: T016's landed watchdog stops calling the script and calls the port directly.
decisions.why: A direct consequence of the port and of FR-003: the caller reaches the one implementation. Nothing asked for is dropped.

decisions.id: (b) the script stays as a forwarder until T051
decisions.summary: finished-run-hooks.sh remains only to run l7r-guard.sh --finished-run for review_prereq.py (phase 3); its hook modes leave the settings in this task.
decisions.why: Sequencing, not a carve-out. The request and FR-001 are about Python; the forwarder holds no Python and no logic, and has a named end at T051. FR-003 holds: only the Rust runs, the forwarder decides nothing. D3 asks that the shell entry leave the settings in the decider's commit, which this does. The premise that review_prereq.py is the only caller does not decide the ruling: the forwarder answers any caller of that path.

decisions.id: (c) the tools it asks stay theirs: lib/writer-alive.sh asked by path until T051
decisions.summary: The port keeps shelling out to the shell helper for each waiter's file.
decisions.why: The helper is described as shell, not Python, so FR-001 does not reach it, and it has a named end at T051. FR-007 (not cited by the block, its first line read in spec-index.md) is one process per GUARD rather than per helper, and finished-run-hooks' guard modes are prompt and stop rather than the before-Bash path SC-001 measures. Premise on record: the block does not say on which modes the helper runs, and within rests on the helper holding no inline Python.

decisions.id: (d)-1 os.access(path, X_OK) restated as the file's execute bits
decisions.summary: A semantic restatement in the port, named by the author, differing from access(2) only where the caller is not the file's owner or is root.
decisions.why: FR-002's bar is 'every case its tests and its suites hold', and the block scopes the difference to what no case tells apart; a divergence no case exercises is inside FR-002 by its words, and it is not named as an exception to anything the GM asked. The premise was read rather than run; D4's replay at exit 6 is the measurement, and a case that does tell them apart turns the exit red.

decisions.id: (d)-2 sort -n | tail -1 restated as newest by mtime, then by path
decisions.summary: The run-log selection expressed directly in Rust.
decisions.why: The same ordering stated in other terms; FR-002 and the D4 replay bind it.

decisions.summary: The goal line, read with (b) and item 9.
decisions.why: Item 9 states the measured form: logic and settings entries gone, the script kept only as (b)'s forwarder until T051. Looser prose in the goal line, not a departure from the request.

decisions.summary: The script's logic and its settings entries go in the commit that registers the decider.
decisions.why: D3 as written, and FR-003's never both.

decisions.summary: After T005 in the plan's order; green on the suite against the Rust guard, make rust-test, cover and hooks-test, red to make arbiter-ask; lands by make land-tooling with no work budget.
decisions.why: Order and process inside D3 and D4; the green exit carries FR-002 (suite) and FR-004 (cover), and nothing the GM asked for is reduced.

decisions.summary: The guard's cheap half (live reviews, live rolls via /proc, the refusal's words) moves in-process in Rust; lib/hm_engine_freeze.py is deleted.
decisions.why: FR-001 puts scripts/hooks/ and its libraries in phase 1; FR-002/D4 hold the verdicts by the suite. The deletion is fully true only together with (b3), which moves the unported glue out rather than porting it; that is ruled at (b3). The block's citation of T052's census is not in the bundle and the decision does not need it: FR-001 alone carries the deletion.

decisions.summary: The two answerers (l7r/diagram/ci/delta.py's engine list, scripts/gates/gate-stamp.py's AST identity) stay Python until phase 2 although a phase-1 guard calls them.
decisions.why: FR-001 reaches these files through two clauses: 'the libraries its guards call - phase 1' and the by-name 'l7r/diagram/ci/, the gate's scripts under scripts/gates/' - phase 2. The block quotes only the second, so this is classed narrowing of phase 1 rather than passed as settled. Legitimate because the spec's own words imply it and the literal alternative breaks the spec: a phase-1 port of delta.py is either the gate's core ported before the gate (against FR-001's stated order and its by-name placement of the whole directory), or the one list ported alone while the phase-2 gate still reads the Python list, which is one piece in two implementations (FR-003, 'no piece runs both'). Purpose test against the GM's words: the request is that all Python be ported and that hook startup cost matters; both files are still ported, SC-005's census cannot close with them present, and the hook's Python cost falls from two starts on every engine edit to starts only while a review or roll is live, for an interim ending at phase 2. The exception does not gut the purpose.

decisions.summary: The Rust guard consults those answerers as a child process, and asks them last, only when a review or roll is live.
decisions.why: FR-007's words are 'one process for a tool call, not one per guard'; a tool consulted by the one guard process is not a process per guard, and that reading stands on FR-007 itself. The quoted T006 decision (a) line is not in the bundle (spec-cited.md lacks it), so it was judged as quoted and not relied on. Asking last reorders a conjunction of questions; the block states the same refused-only-when condition, and FR-002/D4's replay of every suite case is the exit that holds it.

decisions.summary: The glue that loads the answerers (_is_engine, docstring_only) moves from scripts/hooks/ to a new tracked file scripts/gates/engine_edit.py, deleted when phase 2 ports its answerers.

decisions.why: FR-002 requires the same verdicts AND outputs, its named exceptions do not cover this, and the warning is an output, so this is a narrowing and is presumed wrong. It is legitimate on the impossibility leg: the warning reports that a Python decision failed to run, the port leaves no Python decision to fail, and emitting it would state something false. Its purpose, the session being told its guard did not decide, passes to the wrapper's notice (T004) rather than being dropped. The ruling rests on two premises this bundle cannot confirm, the repository being closed to this review. First, the import-stub case asserts the act, as (e) says, and not the warning line; D4 is the backstop, since a case expecting that line fails against l7r-guard --only house-style-hooks and stops the switch, and editing such a case would have to be named as FR-002's exceptions are. Second, 'no import to fail' does not by its own words reach the data file (c) creates: if the table is read at runtime, a missing or malformed file is the failure this warning existed for, and it must then reach the session through T004's notice or be compiled in. Silence on that failure is outside this ruling.

decisions.summary: The suite's import-stub case keeps its assertion that the guard still acts on a command with hm_house.py broken, now by driving the link with the module broken in a copy of the tree; its verdict does not change.

'Never a plain Bash call or Edit' is a claim about which events reach these branches, not measured in the bundle and taken as stated; the ruling does not rest on it. decisions.id: item-1/item-6/(d) the goal read as a plain Bash call
decisions.summary: SC-001 ('the guards before a Bash call') is restated as 'a plain Bash call', and the green exit is m:t054-plain-bash under 17.5 ms, while (d) concedes a command with quotes or git still compiles what it needs and the entry records it at quoted_git_ms 29.43-29.73 against target_ms 17.5.
decisions.why: The word 'plain' is not in SC-001; the plan inserted it. The pointer m:hooks-bash in SC-001 supplies the baseline (175 ms, so 17.5), not the scope of calls: that the baseline was sampled on an ls does not make ls the only call the criterion speaks of, and reading it so is completing the thought. Item (d) discloses the gap honestly, but disclosure is not a ruling. Against the tests: not physically impossible (the block does not argue 29 to 17.5 cannot be done); not implied by the GM's words (request.md says nothing about commands that match no pattern; it says hook startup time matters and the Python is too inefficient); the literal reading does not defeat the purpose, it IS the purpose, whereas fast exits that fire only on commands no rule could match meet the number on the instrument's own sample and leave any call with a quote or a git over it. How much of real Bash traffic is plain is unmeasured. CLEAR would need either: item 1 drops 'plain' and item 6 requires both recorded commands under 17.5 ms; or the block names this as an exception to SC-001 and takes it to make arbiter-ask rather than ticking on the plain figure.

decisions.why: D7 of the accepted spec settles the wrapper, and FR-007's one process per tool call is about guards, not the launcher. Its stated reason, 'the target is met', holds only on the plain figure and falls with the narrowing above; keeping the wrapper does not.

decisions.why: FR-001 carries this verbatim (ask:449-T76-scope, 'no door', expected remainders, T065 clause). The widened grep now covers the importers and the shell and Rust entry points, which answers the clause.

decisions.summary: tool_yield.py also goes to phase 3, the seventh, because fix_yield.py still imports it.
decisions.why: FR-001's ruling names six; a seventh leaves phase 2. The rule cannot be followed here: a Python module cannot be replaced by Rust while a Python importer survives, and keeping both is what FR-003 forbids. It is deferred, not excused: T065 clause, named in the phase-2 close, and SC-005's census still closes on it. The premise that fix_yield.py imports it is stated with no method and could not be checked from this bundle.

decisions.summary: A usage line names the new command instead of the Python's.
decisions.why: FR-002 says same outputs. Matching would print the name of a deleted file as the way to run the tool, which defeats what a usage line is for. No verdict or exit status moves.

decisions.summary: guard-log lists firings of the same second in file order where the Python's glob gave the file system's.
decisions.why: The Python's tie order is whatever the file system returns, so it has no one value across clones and no test can hold it; FR-002 binds every case the tests and suites hold, and those are replayed. Only the order of ties moves, not which firings are listed.

decisions.summary: fresh-tally lists causes tied on a count in name order where the Python iterated a set.
decisions.why: The Python's order changes from run to run, so it disagrees with itself and 'the same output' has no referent. Physically impossible to match; a fixed order is the only faithful port.

decisions.summary: shared_text, contract_part, contract_shared and their _lines move into tests/tooling/test_bundle_shared_text.py rather than being ported with subagent_cache.py.
decisions.why: Their stated only caller is a Python test, and a Python test cannot import a Rust function, so FR-001's 'each tests/ file with the piece it tests' carries them with it. The bodies are unchanged and remain in both censuses until that file goes, so FR-002 replaces nothing here and nothing leaves the port. The grep is now named and sees imports, but its pathspec omits specs/, which FR-001 counts; a harness there would break at the deletion, a correctness risk for the landing and not a fidelity ruling.

decisions.summary: The listed cases of the slice's test files are replayed in measure/*/tests.rs.
decisions.why: This is FR-002's requirement and FR-008's test home, applied to the slice.

decisions.summary: test_runstats.py keeps the cases of tests/_gate_failures.py and of the Makefile's wiring, in Python.
decisions.why: A test of a ported tool's file outlives the tool, which on its face departs from porting it. FR-001's own words place it: each tests/ file goes with the piece it tests, and _gate_failures.py stays Python with pytest, which FR-001 ends in phase 4. The file stays in the census and SC-005 closes on it.

decisions.summary: Every specs/*/measurements*.json command running a file this task ports or deletes is rewritten in the same commit to the port and re-run.
decisions.why: FR-001 requires exactly this.

decisions.summary: The five measure tools become l7r-gate measure subcommands in one landing; the Makefile and three figure files are rewritten, and docs/spec-kit-and-reviews.md's model_trial step and rust/phases/src/driver/CLAUDE.md's pointer with them.
decisions.why: FR-001 places these files through ask:449-T068-scope, model_trial.py, popup_rounds.py and push_check_times.py in the last slice, and names the docs step. Changed since last judged: the two documents are now rewritten with the port. The search spaces are stated.

decisions.id: THE DELETION WAITS ON THE GM
decisions.summary: The ports land first; the removal of the five tools and two tests was refused by the built-in safety check, so the task stays open until the GM runs it; the two tests that import the tools stay and pass until then.
decisions.why: Nothing asked for is dropped: the exits and item 9 still require the files gone and the task cannot close without it. FR-002 binds the port before the deletion. On FR-003's 'no piece runs both': recipes, hooks and figures run only the port, and the Python's only remaining run is its own two tests, which test it and do not serve the piece. Changed since last judged: 'nothing invokes the Python' is replaced by this exact statement.

decisions.summary: replay_owing.py and depiction_replay.py go to phase 3 with modal_owed, modal_triage and claims; the other deferred tools as FR-001 and T070's row place them.
decisions.why: FR-001 carries ask:449-T77-replays and ask:449-T77-scope. Each file is still ported or deleted under the request's own terms; only its phase moves.

decisions.summary: model_trial.rs holds a Rust fold_usage, and agent_census.py's phase-3 port calls that one.
decisions.why: FR-003's unit is the piece: model-trial usage runs the Rust fold and agent_census.py, unported until phase 3, runs its Python one; neither runs both. The 40-transcript differential is the plan's stated proof. The spec's record of ask:449-T77-replays does not name fold_usage, so this rests on FR-003, not on that record.

decisions.summary: One-shot differentials of each command through the Python and the binary over the real repository.
decisions.why: FR-002's reach is every case the tests and suites hold, carried by WHAT THE TESTS REPLAY. The differentials are proof beyond that reach and take nothing from it; that run and run-all are not among them, and that usage is a seeded sample of 40, does not lower it.

decisions.id: DIFFERENCE: run in a process group
decisions.summary: run starts each session in its own process group, not its own session.
decisions.why: FR-002 binds verdicts and outputs, the line the spec's own ask:449-T77-bad-since draws. Which process session a launched child sits in is neither, and the plan states the only effect is the controlling terminal. This ground stands alone: the plan's remark about the standard library is a cost argument and is not relied on.

decisions.summary: A bad --since to popup-rounds exits 1 with empty stdout and one stderr line naming the value; which values parse, and the local-time conversion, stay the Python's.
decisions.why: Exactly FR-002's ruled case ask:449-T77-bad-since. Changed since last judged: 'refused where the Python raised' is replaced by the ruled shape, with a labeled one-shot differential over 13,876 forms showing which values parse.

decisions.summary: run-all's progress times read the local zone, as the Python's did.
decisions.why: Sameness with the Python, which FR-002 asks. Changed since last judged: the earlier block's UTC difference is gone.

decisions.summary: The Rust rows are the Rust push's CHECKS table plus the one-process run; the proof is m:push-checks-rust.
decisions.why: FR-001 names it an FR-002 ruled case under ask:449-T77-scope with that proof over the Rust push's table, and the commands the Python listed are of a shell line already removed, so the tool still measures the push as it now is.

decisions.summary: Every case of test_maps_moved.py and test_model_trial.py is in measure/*/tests.rs.
decisions.why: This is FR-002's own requirement carried out.

decisions.summary: git ls-files names none of the slice's files; every measurements command running a ported or deleted file is rewritten in the same commit and re-run.

decisions.summary: the gate's inline Python becomes l7r-gate log run/bypass/gate-bypass/land-tooling, ruff-toml and json-field in rust/gate/src/logs.rs
decisions.why: FR-001's second census puts the Makefile's gate recipes, scripts/gates/*.sh, sync-with-main.sh and land-tooling.sh in phase 2; unchanged since last judged.

decisions.summary: python3 -m pip show -q pytest-xdist replaces the import probe, the serial arm stays, and it goes with the pytest line in phase 4, named at the phase-2 close by its own search
decisions.why: FR-001 carries ask:449-T069-xdist in these terms, so placement is not reopened. Both arms measured 2026-11-09, method: the two probes run under python3 and python3 -s, -s hiding the user-site xdist with the system pip still visible. Present: both exit 0. Absent, the real package name: both exit 1, so the probe forks as the import did and 'the same question' holds on both arms. The two differ only on an interpreter without pip (the import can succeed, pip show cannot), which falls to the serial arm: a slower run, same verdict.

decisions.id: XDIST PROBE: the T065 clause's last limb
decisions.summary: the probe holds the clause on a plain Bash call, a plain Edit, Makefile parse time and an already-verified make done, but still runs on every other make done, including one picking no Python test, until T071 and phase 4
decisions.why: FR-001 says the probe carries the T065 clause and the block concedes one limb, so this is a narrowing whether or not it is labeled one. Limb by limb: Bash call, Edit, parse time and already-verified are held and excepted from nothing. The make-done limb cannot be held inside the ruled form: the ruling fixes a probe that is itself a Python start on the pytest line, and that line runs on every make done that passes already-verified, so while the line runs the probe runs. The exception is the physically-impossible case, not an awkward one, and it does not gut the clause's purpose, since the same recipe starts python3 -m l7r.diagram.ci incremental and pytest on that make done regardless. It ends where the block says, at T071 and phase 4. The premise that done always reaches test-full is the block's one-shot reading of the Makefile dated 2026-11-09; the bundle bars re-reading the repository, so it was weighed as labeled and not re-measured.

decisions.summary: test-cohort-gate, test-land-tooling and test-claims-gate's index edit use jq; test-entry-gate's edit is a literal shell replacement
decisions.why: ask:449-T052-inline-census moves these four suites to phase 2, and removing their inline Python is what that asks; unchanged since last judged.

decisions.summary: make audit's four recipes, buildspec/run.sh until T73, and the two fixtures over claims.py and record_owed.py remain after T069
decisions.why: Each is placed by the accepted spec: FR-001's ask:449-T069-suites names the two fixtures and make audit's four recipes with their phases, and FR-001a deletes buildspec. Unchanged since last judged.

decisions.summary: a record's bytes are the Python's, numbers included: logs.rs's dumps writes json.dumps's form and a float as repr writes it, each form pinned by a test, no exception
decisions.why: FR-002 held whole. The earlier text excepted serde's exponent form on a one-shot grep of existing logs; that exception is gone and the block says so. The rule governs every form, not only the parenthetical's examples. Python 3.14 measured 2026-11-09, method: json.dumps on each value: 5e-05, 1e+16, 1e+22, 0.0001, 1.0, -0.0, 1.2345678901234568e+17, DEL escaped as backslash-u007f, non-BMP as a surrogate pair, NaN and Infinity written bare, and an integer past 64 bits written whole. The tests should pin those too.

decisions.summary: the census's phase-2 share prints only What stays' sites; measurement commands running a ported or deleted file are rewritten and re-run in the same commit
decisions.why: FR-001's second census over the phase-2 set and the four suites, and FR-001's rule on recorded measurements; unchanged since last judged. The probe is outside this pattern, which does not match -m, and the XDIST block assigns it its own search.

decisions.summary: T071 is preflight.py alone; the test planner's files are out of it (goal, exits and Done rewritten to that).
decisions.why: FR-001's ask:449-T071-scope replaces T067's placement: selection, incremental, cover_changed and the rest go in phase 4, preflight.py is ported in T071. The earlier block's planner exit and its no-.py-under-ci measure are gone.

decisions.summary: l7r-gate preflight holds the derived files, the record, the quick tier, the stray-probe refusal, the snapshot, the check, what the gate rolled and the gate-write guard's question; the Makefile's four calls and gate_write_hooks.rs call it.
decisions.why: This is the port FR-001 orders in phase 2 for preflight.py, called once a process per FR-006.

decisions.summary: scripts/gates/preflight.py stays at its path, cut to --cover (changed lines' coverage), asked only by make preflight, gone in phase 4 with pytest.
decisions.why: FR-001: 'preflight.py is ported in T071, its pytest-reading checks behind one named door until phase 4'. --cover reads coverage.py's data and is the only thing left behind the door; the earlier block's Python-reading --same-py is no longer in it.

decisions.summary: make done passes --no-coverage, as the Python's make done did (feature 405 T47, D25), so no make done starts the door.
decisions.why: Stated as preserving existing behavior, which FR-002 requires; that premise is the plan's and cannot be measured from this bundle. If the Python's make done did not already skip it, this is a behavior change owing its own FR-002 case. It starts less Python than FR-001 permits, not more.

decisions.summary: The two-version question (does a .py file's two versions differ only where the gate does not look) is a new verb --same-program on codeid.py, one batch, at most once a run, only when a .py file outside the byte-hashed areas changed.
decisions.why: Classed narrowing because FR-001 lets only preflight.py's pytest-reading checks stay Python and this check is not one; the spec names --debug-free-equal on codeid.py and does not name this verb. Against the request ('should probably all be ported to Rust ... making this a Rust codebase'): nothing leaves the port's scope, the question is about Python source, codeid.py goes in phase 4 and SC-005's censuses must return nothing, so it ends with the last .py. FR-002 binds the answer to the Python's, and the reference is CPython's own parser, the class FR-001 already settled for codeid.py (ask:449-T062-py-id, its .py id is Python's own ast.dump, asked by the Rust gate by path; --debug-free-equal the same). Purpose: the request came from measured Python cost on hooks and a one-line Rust edit's make done; a Rust edit moves no .py file, so the SC-002 case starts none.

decisions.summary: The verb may start from the gate-write guard, on an Edit while a gate is running and such a file changed.
decisions.why: Adjudicated apart from the make done branch. FR-001 forbids codeid.py on a plain Bash call or a plain Edit; the spec's own engine_edit.py clause reads plain Edit as one 'with none live', and ask:449-phase1-tools-by-path allows a rare branch. With no gate running the block starts nothing, so a plain Edit starts no Python.

decisions.summary: The verb may start on the tree check of a make done whose tree moved such a file.
decisions.why: Adjudicated apart from the guard branch. It matches the FR-001 T065 clause's shape (no Python on a make done whose change holds no file it reads) and is one process for the run; a Rust-only change never reaches it, which is the case the request's cost complaint and SC-002 name.

decisions.summary: hamlet_path's import of l7r.diagram.tools.claims stays inside --cover, reached only by make preflight, Python by path until phase 3, never on a make done.
decisions.why: Under FR-001's ask:449-T067-scope ceiling ('staying Python by path until phase 3 and only on a make done whose change holds a file claims reads'); never on a make done is stricter than that ceiling and narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: raw_areas asks the stamp's --raw-match as the Python did, so a page_browser docstring edit is called as before; any correction goes through its own case.
decisions.why: FR-002: same verdicts by default, with the correction route it names.

decisions.summary: --cover's JSON answer is new, between the Rust and Python halves; each line the phase prints is the Python's.
decisions.why: An internal interface that exists only because of the door FR-001 orders; FR-002 binds the printed output, which is held.

decisions.summary: The phase's and tree's cases move to preflight/tests.rs; the door's stay in test_preflight.py, with one new case for --cover and one for --same-program.
decisions.why: FR-001 'each tests/ file with the piece it tests'; the two new cases only test what this task changes.

decisions.summary: Done is the differential over the real repository with no mismatch, preflight.py holding only --cover and what it calls, and every recorded measurement command naming a ported or deleted file rewritten and re-run in the same commit.
decisions.why: FR-002's same-verdicts requirement and FR-001's recorded-measurement clause, nearly word for word.

decisions.summary: Leaf first by imports, callers reach the binary once a process or in a batch; a red exit goes to make arbiter-ask; no work budget.
decisions.why: ask:449-T062-order, FR-006, SC-002 and the arbiter's standing role; the budget line settles nothing the request addressed.

decisions.summary: Under tests/ only ten named test files, the six modules they and pytest load, and the non-Python directories stay; every other Python test is deleted.
decisions.why: The GM said 'delete everything except that group', and FR-001b records the group by subject (the sweep of the hand-drawn sheets and the checks of agent files, CLAUDE.md files and other documents) and delegates naming it to this plan. Each of the ten is one of those by name; the six helpers are what makes them loadable. The bundle does not hold the group as it was shown to the GM, so membership is checked against FR-001b's record of it, not against that text.

decisions.summary: selection.py, gate_plugin.py, incremental.py, pool_readers.py, gate_config.py's two readers, scripts/gates/pool-readers.py, cover_changed.py, refresh_baseline.py and preflight.py are deleted here rather than in the commit removing pytest; the kept suite runs whole with no selection and no coverage.
decisions.why: FR-001b settles it: the planner and the coverage floor over Python go with the tests, in place of ask:449-T071-scope's commit. With them gone a whole run of the kept group is the only remaining form, and the GM exempted that group from the deletion.

decisions.summary: check-function-cap.py, check-duplicate-defs.py, ruff format, pyrefly and check stale-dirs are deleted.
decisions.why: The GM asked which static checks on the Python can go away and approved the answer ('Sounds good, please proceed with that'); FR-001b carries it. Nothing here retains or adds a check. The approved list itself is not in the bundle.

decisions.summary: The .py arm of check file-scale's line bar goes; the .rs bar and the per-directory file count stay.
decisions.why: The only text changed since the BLOCKED round. The earlier block kept the bar whole by calling the list's 'Python-file size bar' a mislabel, which completed the GM's thought against what was approved. This block deletes the part the approved list named. The .rs bar and the directory count are not checks on the Python, so keeping them narrows nothing the GM asked about.

decisions.summary: ruff check stays, narrowed to E9, F63, F7 and F82.
decisions.why: Taken against the request and not only the spec: the GM's words were a question, 'which of our static checks ... can also go away now?', so a list leaving one standing does not contradict them, and FR-001b records 'ruff check stays, narrowed to outright errors' under the GM's approval of that answer. The plan's four rule families only spell out 'outright errors'. It keeps no behavior the GM asked to change, and it does reduce what the check reports. Item 1's goal sentence reads more broadly than this and is loosely worded; the decision is the operative text.

decisions.summary: The commit before the removal is tagged python-tests-before-removal so a port can read the cases it replays; new Rust still owes 100% line coverage.
decisions.why: The tag removes nothing and preserves nothing in the tree: the deletion the GM asked for still happens. It is how FR-002's 'on every case its tests and its suites hold' stays reachable after the tests are gone. The coverage clause restates FR-004.

decisions.summary: Tag, then delete the tests and Python-only tooling in one commit with the Makefile, land.py, the guards and the crates edited to stop reading them.
decisions.why: The GM: 'if literally any of our tests or gates required that to work, we can edit them to no longer run unit tests on any of the Python stuff.' The edits are limited to what stops reading the deleted things.

decisions.summary: Green is make done, quick, land and hooks-test on only the kept tests; red goes to make arbiter-ask; done is git ls-files showing only kept files, no recipe naming a deleted tool, and make done's time recorded against m:done-rust-edit.
decisions.why: Each check only fails when the requested deletion is absent or broke the gate, so it enforces the request. The recorded time is the measurement FR-010 and SC-002 already require.

decisions.summary: Phase 2 closes with SC-002 recorded NOT MET (22.0 s against 15.1 s), its shares named in dev/, the line unmoved and re-measured at the phase-3 close.
decisions.why: SC-002 is not phase-scoped and is not relaxed: its line stays and is measured again. What binds a phase end is FR-010 (measure against the spec's figures, record in dev/), which this does. The shares change only because FR-001b removed the planner the ruling named; pytest 4 s, preflight 5 s and seeds 8 s cover the 6.9 s gap. The arbiter's quoted ruling is not in the bundle beyond FR-001/FR-001b's references to it, and m: figures were taken as labeled, not re-run, because the MANIFEST forbids reading the repository.

decisions.summary: The preflight stands aside on a verified tree, so make done's already-verified path starts no test.
decisions.why: This is SC-002's second half; m:done-unchanged-after records tests_run 0.

decisions.summary: A make done is judged at the existing 5 s incremental floor instead of the 40 s floor of the pinned ratchet baseline; neither setting's value moves.
decisions.why: It narrows nothing the GM asked for, and the request's purpose is a faster loop. SC-002 requires under 15.1 s, which is below a 40 s floor, so keeping that floor would refuse every run that meets SC-002. Item 10 now says this openly in place of the earlier 'None moved'. FR-002 is port equivalence and FR-006 appears only as a first line; neither visibly holds this floor, which the bundle cannot settle further. Noted for the record: the reach is every make done, including one that reuses no crate's checks, where the stated reason does not apply; no clause of the request or cited requirement speaks to that case.

decisions.summary: With test_rust_tooling.py deleted by FR-001b, FR-008's one end-to-end test is rustc/tests.rs's the_real_cargo_tests_a_real_crate.
decisions.why: It names which test fills the one end-to-end place FR-008 allows; the real cargo over a fixture crate is a test against the real command.

decisions.summary: The .py census's phase-2 share is a stated pathspec, now including switches.py and hm_conflict.py; the second census's remainder is the four make audit recipes and the two T069-suites fixtures; the xdist probe is gone by its own search.
decisions.why: The pathspec now holds FR-001's phase-2 locations and the phase-2 library hm_conflict.py; own-make.sh is a shell file and outside the .py census. The xdist clause meets FR-001's 'named at the phase-2 close by its own search', at the Makefile gate recipe FR-001 names. The second-census clause carries no command, filter or date of its own, but it narrows nothing: FR-001 defines that census by an exact git grep and assigns its phase-2 sites, FR-001 itself names these six as what the close names, and items 6 and 9 run both censuses and read the phase-2 share. Its loose wording is a drafting point, not a narrowing. The census results were not re-run (no repository reads).

decisions.summary: size_table.py and open_questions.py go in phase 4 with the Mode A code they import, carrying the T065 clause and named at the phase-3 close (ask:449-T79-moves).
decisions.why: Item (a). FR-001 now names both files by path, the ruling, the phase, the clause and the phase-3 close, and the block says the same. Only their order moves: they are still ported, as the GM's 2026-11-07 request wants.

decisions.summary: specs/251 seeded.py and run_seeded.sh are deleted, not ported.
decisions.why: Item (b). FR-001 names both files deleted, not ported, under the GM's 2026-11-09 words 'I don't think we need to port the past feature harnesses if those are not still used', which also stand in request.md.

decisions.summary: The block cites ask:449-T79-moves with the search as now run (ast walk of tracked .py, word-bounded grep over Makefile, .sh and rust/, whole-tree grep of seeded.py and run_seeded) and records that seeded.py's by-path load names scripts/_agent_census.py, which is no tracked file.
decisions.why: Item (c). The grounds for 'not still used' are stated with their dated one-shot methods and the ask cited; the earlier text's narrower grep is gone. The ruling closes the search, so its reach was not reopened.

decisions.summary: docs/spec-kit-and-reviews.md:109 is rewritten in the removal commit to name scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh measure model-trial in place of seeded.py.
decisions.why: Item (d). The done line carries it. It follows from deleting the harness, so no document directs a deleted file, and FR-001 already has model_trial ported as the step that document directs.

decisions.summary: Seven tools become l7r-gate record verbs with one port of SequenceMatcher.
decisions.why: Unchanged since the last reading. FR-001 phase 3 and the request's port of all Python.

decisions.summary: Libraries with Python importers move to T81, T82 and T83 with their callers; agent_sync.py goes in T83 with its kept test.
decisions.why: Unchanged since the last reading. Ordering inside phase 3 so one implementation runs (FR-003); the kept test follows FR-001b.

decisions.summary: Each verb is compared with its Python; agent-census's one difference is the command lines --record writes, which name the verb.
decisions.why: Unchanged since the last reading. FR-002 requires the same outputs, FR-001 requires recorded commands to name the port, and FR-001b holds still-running Python by each port's differential.

decisions.summary: review_round_hooks asks l7r-gate record stale-dirs in place of its inline Python.
decisions.why: Unchanged since the last reading. FR-001's second census: an inline site follows the piece it belongs to.

decisions.summary: The Python files stay until the GM approves their removal; no recipe, hook or figure runs them meanwhile.
decisions.why: Unchanged since the last reading. It only delays deletion, and removes nothing from what was asked; FR-003 holds that no piece runs both.

decisions.why: The GM asked that the Python all be ported to Rust; FR-001's ruled order (ask:449-T80-order) names exactly this slice in one cut.

decisions.summary: partial-citations keeps its delta gate, only the files it reads named anew.
decisions.why: FR-002 binds verdicts and outputs, and keeping the delta gate moves neither; the input path names are not an output. Whether the renamed list is complete cannot be checked from the bundle (the MANIFEST forbids the repository), and nothing in the block claims a narrower reach.

decisions.why: Serves FR-003 (no piece runs both) while those callers wait for step 3 of ask:449-T80-order. The census states its search space (an ast walk of every tracked .py for imports and importlib/by-path strings, dated one-shot).

decisions.why: FR-001's ruled order paragraph carries this finding nearly verbatim (both ported in-process through the flock(1) helper T014 decided, ingest by path until step 3). It removes Python sooner than the older by-path wording allowed, so it moves toward the request.

decisions.summary: today asks date(1) for the local date, as Python's date.today() does, not the UTC clock.
decisions.why: FR-002: the same outputs as the Python replaced.

decisions.summary: The verdicts are held by a differential of each command through Python and binary on the real repository and two scratch clones (249 comparisons, 0 differences, one-shot, observed 2026-11-10); argparse usage text and a Python traceback's text are not compared, citing ask:449-usage-text.
decisions.why: The request does not ask for byte-equal parser text, and FR-002 carries ask:449-usage-text as a ruled case. The exclusion stays inside that ruling's seam: only stderr argparse generates and an uncaught traceback's text are unbound; exit status and stdout stay held and are among what was compared; a parser.error message, a hand-written usage line or refusal, usage text read by a caller and --help held by a kept suite case stay bound, and the block claims none of those excluded. The figure carries a date and method as a one-shot label; it was not re-run because the MANIFEST forbids the repository. The doubled sentence is a drafting wart, not a fidelity finding.
